newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia money supply growth mixed in Sept.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia money supply growth mixed in Sept.

text.p: The annual growth rate of all three Malaysian monetary aggregates were mixed in September, with broad money or M3 showing an annual 21.1 percent growth versus a 21.8 pct gain in August, Bank Negara said on Monday.
Note: M1 - money in circulation and cash on deposit in banks
M2 - M1 plus time, savings and foreign currency deposits
On a month-to-month basis, narrow money, M1, rose by 2.4 billion ringgit or 4.3 percent after a decline of 987 million ringgit or 1.7 percent in August.
This was mainly due to the strong growth in demand deposits of 2.7 billion ringgit or 7.4 percent during the month.

On a monthly basis, growth of M2 was virtually unchanged at 2.6 billion ringgit or 1.2 percent versus August's rise of 2.7 billion ringgit or 1.2 percent. Bank Negara attributed this to a decline in repos and a much slower pace of growth in fixed deposits after a sharp rise in August.
Broad money or M3 was boosted by an increase in private sector deposits which rose by 1.3 billion ringgit compared with a gain of 556 million ringgit in August.
That led to a month-on-month gain in M3 of 3.9 billion ringgit or 1.3 percent in September. In August, broad money grew by 3.2 billion ringgit or 1.1 percent.
